---
title: "Try Free AI Demos in Your Browser with Hugging Face Spaces"
subtitle: "Explore hundreds of community-built AI tools for images, text, and audio, and run them instantly in your web browser without any installation or coding."
category: "guide"
audience: "both"
company: "Hugging Face"
tool: "Hugging Face"
level: "beginner"
read_time_minutes: 6
tags: ["getting-started", "ai-demos", "hugging-face"]
---

Have you ever wanted to try out the latest AI tools, like those that can create images from text or summarise long documents, without needing to install anything complicated? Hugging Face Spaces is like a giant, free online playground where people share their interactive AI creations. By the end of this guide, you'll know how to explore this amazing collection and run various AI demonstrations (demos) directly in your web browser, giving you a hands-on feel for what AI can do.

## Before you start
-   A device with a web browser (computer, tablet, or smartphone).
-   An internet connection.
-   Access to Hugging Face Spaces is free for trying out demos.
-   Rough total time: 5-10 minutes for your first exploration.

## Step 1 — Visit Hugging Face Spaces
First, let's open up the Hugging Face Spaces website in your browser. This website hosts a vast collection of AI demonstrations.
You'll see a homepage often featuring popular or newly trending "Spaces," which is what Hugging Face calls these individual AI demo apps. There's usually a search bar at the top and categories like "Image," "Text," or "Audio" to help you filter.
After typing the address, your browser will load the Hugging Face Spaces main page, showing a grid or list of various AI demo apps.
If it looks different, don't worry! Websites often update their design. Just look for a clear heading like "Spaces" or "Demos" and a prominent search bar.
You'll know it worked when you see a page filled with square or rectangular cards, each representing a different AI application, and a search bar near the top.

## Step 2 — Discover an AI Demo
Now that you're on the Spaces homepage, let's find an AI demo that interests you. Think of these "Spaces" as individual mini-apps, each showcasing a specific AI skill, like a tiny tool you can play with.
Look for the search bar, usually at the top or centre of the page, and type in a keyword like "image generation" or "summarise text." You can also browse by clicking on category filters if they are available.
When you click on a demo card, or press Enter after searching, you'll be taken to that specific Space's page. This page will host the interactive AI tool itself.
If you can't find anything specific, try clicking on a "Trending" or "Popular" demo from the main page to see what others are using.
You'll know it worked when you land on a new page dedicated to one AI demo, with a title describing its function and usually an interactive area where you can input information.

## Step 3 — Understand the Demo Interface
Once you've selected an AI demo, it's time to get familiar with its controls. Each demo, or "Space," is a unique web application created by a developer, but they often share common elements.
You'll typically see one or more input fields (boxes where you can type text or upload files) and a "Submit" or "Generate" button. Some demos might have sliders or dropdown menus to adjust settings, like the `creativity` of an image generator or the `length` of a summary. There might also be a small description of what the AI does.
After looking over the interface, you'll have a good idea of what kind of information the AI expects from you and what options you can change.
If it looks confusing, scroll down a bit. Many Spaces include instructions or examples from their creators. If you see a complex field, just focus on the main text input for now.
You'll know it worked when you can identify where you're meant to type or upload something, and you can see a clear button to trigger the AI's action.

## Step 4 — Provide Your Input
This is where you tell the AI what you want it to do! Depending on the demo you chose, your input will vary. An AI "model" is the core brain doing the work, and it needs instructions, often called a "prompt," to know what to produce.
For a text summariser, you'll copy and paste text. For an image generator, you'll type a description. If it's a voice cloning tool, you might need to upload a short audio clip. Find the main input box or upload area.
Once you've entered your information, the AI is ready to process your request.
If the input area asks for a specific file type (e.g., "Upload .png image") and you try to upload something else, the demo might show an error. Just make sure your input matches what the demo is looking for.
You'll know it worked when your text is in the input box, or your file has successfully uploaded, and the "Submit" or "Generate" button becomes active.
💬 Example (for an image generator): `a fluffy cat wearing sunglasses, lounging on a beach under a palm tree, cartoon style`

## Step 5 — Run the AI
With your input ready, it's time to activate the AI! This process is called "inference," which is when the AI takes your request and generates an output.
Look for a button labelled something like "Submit," "Generate," "Run," or "Go." Click this button to send your input to the AI model.
After clicking, the demo might show a "Loading," "Processing," or "Waiting" message, often with a spinning wheel or a progress bar. This means the AI is doing its work. Then, your results will appear on the screen.
If nothing seems to happen after you click, try waiting a few extra seconds. Some complex AI models take a little longer to process, especially if the servers are busy. You might also want to check your internet connection.
You'll know it worked when the "Processing" message disappears, and a new section of the page displays the AI's output, whether it's generated text, an image, or an audio file.

## Step 6 — Review the Results
Finally, let's look at what the AI created! The output section of the demo will show you the result of your "inference" — the AI's response to your input.
You'll see the generated text, image, or audio file, usually displayed clearly below the input area. Many demos also offer options to download the result, or sometimes even share it.
This step completes your first interaction with an AI demo on Hugging Face Spaces! You can now experiment further by changing your input or trying another demo.
If the result isn't what you expected, don't worry. AI can sometimes "hallucinate" (make things up confidently) or simply misinterpret your instruction. This is normal. Try rephrasing your input or adding more detail in the input box, just like you would with a human.
You'll know it worked when you clearly see the AI's generated content on the screen, reflecting your prompt.

## Common mistakes
-   **Not understanding what the demo does**: Some demos have very specific functions.
    *   **The fix**: Read the demo's description carefully or look at the example inputs provided by the creator. If it's still unclear, choose a different, simpler demo.
-   **Providing the wrong type of input**: Trying to upload an image to a text-only summariser, for example.
    *   **The fix**: Always check the labels on the input fields. If it says "Enter text," provide text. If it says "Upload image," ensure you're uploading an image file.
-   **Expecting instant results for complex tasks**: Some AI models, especially those generating high-quality images or long pieces of text, can take a minute or two to process.
    *   **The fix**: Be patient! If a demo seems slow, give it some time. If it still doesn't respond after a few minutes, the demo might be experiencing high traffic or be temporarily offline, so you might need to try a different one.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** Hugging Face Spaces offers a quick, free way to explore the capabilities of various AI tools without any commitment. You can generate fun images for personal projects, summarise articles for your studies, or even experiment with AI voices, all from your browser. It's a fantastic resource for curiosity and casual experimentation.
-   **For your business or work:** You can quickly prototype ideas or test different AI approaches for tasks like marketing copy generation, simple data analysis summaries, or creating unique visual assets. It's an excellent way to see what's possible before investing in more complex, integrated AI solutions.
-   **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to visit Hugging Face Spaces, look for a demo labelled "Image Generation" or "Text Summarizer," and try giving it a simple instruction. Don't be afraid to experiment!

## Try it now
Open your web browser, go to `huggingface.co/spaces`, and in the search bar, type "image generator." Click on one of the popular results and try to generate an image based on a short description, like "a colourful parrot wearing a tiny hat." See what the AI comes up with!
